literal: At the beginning of Yong'an of Wei, he was made metropolitan commandant defending the city of Ling Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an of Wei, he was made metropolitan commandant defending the city of Ling Province.

literal: Yuwen Tai gave him the rank of Grand General of the Guard; Feng would not accept it, so Yuwen sent troops to besiege him but could not take the city.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai offered him the rank of grand general of the guard; Feng refused, and Yuwen sent troops to besiege him but could not take the city.

literal: Feng greatly admired Gao Huan's prestige and virtue and thereupon led several tens of thousands of households to come over.
idiomatic: Feng had long admired Gao Huan's prestige and virtue; he thereupon led several tens of thousands of households to defect.

literal: Gao Huan promoted Feng to General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Southern Fen Province.
idiomatic: Gao Huan promoted Feng to general who pacifies the west and governor of Southern Fen Province.

literal: He then joined the generals on punitive campaigns and pacified bandit disorder.
idiomatic: He then campaigned with the generals and pacified the bandit disorders.

literal: He again followed Gao Huan in defeating Yuwen Tai at Heyin; Feng's merit was greatest, and Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: He again followed Gao Huan in defeating Yuwen Tai at Heyin; Feng's merit stood first, and Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.

literal: He entered court as left guard general and went out as governor of Yin Province.
idiomatic: He entered court as left guard general and went out as governor of Yin Province.

literal: Wang Sizheng held Changshe; Gao Cheng ordered Feng and Prince of Qinghe Yue to attack him.
idiomatic: Wang Sizheng held Changshe; Gao Cheng ordered Feng and Prince of Qinghe Yue to attack him.

literal: Feng devised a plan of water assault and dammed the Wei River to flood the city; as the waters rose, fish and turtles swam there.
idiomatic: Feng devised a water assault: they dammed the Wei River to flood the city, and as the waters rose, fish and turtles swam in the streets.

literal: From the ninth month to the fourth month, the city was on the verge of falling.
idiomatic: From the ninth month to the fourth month the city was on the verge of falling.

literal: Feng and mobile-office commissioner Murong Shaozong saw a white vapor in the north and entered a boat together. Suddenly a violent wind came from the northeast; at high noon it grew dark, sand flew and stones dashed; the boat cables snapped at once, and they drifted to the foot of the city.
idiomatic: Feng and mobile-office commissioner Murong Shaozong saw a white vapor in the north and boarded a boat together. Suddenly a violent wind rose from the northeast; at high noon the sky went dark, sand flew and stones scoured the air, the mooring lines snapped, and the boat was driven to the foot of the city.

literal: Feng swam toward an earthen hill but was driven by the waves and did not arrive in time; men of the west hooked him with poles, and both were killed by the enemy.
idiomatic: Feng swam toward an earthen hill but was beaten by the waves and could not reach it in time; Western troops hooked him with poles, and both were killed by the enemy.

literal: Feng was stalwart, brave, and skilled in battle, and was acclaimed by the generals.
idiomatic: Feng was stalwart, brave, and skilled in battle, and the generals held him in high esteem.

literal: On the day he died, court and countryside alike were struck with dismay and lament.
idiomatic: On the day he died, court and countryside alike were struck with dismay and grief.

literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Marshal, Duke of the Department of State Affairs, Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous title Zhong.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, duke of the department of state affairs, and director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous title Loyal.

literal: His son Ye succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Ye succeeded.

literal: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu Shanyu.
idiomatic: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu shanyu.

literal: Right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name; later men garbled it into Poliuhan.
idiomatic: The right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name, and later men garbled it into Poliuhan.

literal: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque inherited the chieftaincy in succession.
idiomatic: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque had inherited the chieftaincy in turn.

literal: Kongque was from youth fierce and brave.
idiomatic: Kongque was fierce and brave from youth.

literal: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, Director of State Affairs, and Prince Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, director of state affairs, and prince who pacifies the south.

literal: Kongque led his division, ten thousand men, and submitted to Erzhu Rong; an edict added General Who Pacifies the North and chief of the first tribally enrolled division; he died.
idiomatic: Kongque led his division of ten thousand men and submitted to Erzhu Rong; an edict added general who pacifies the north and chief of the first tribally enrolled division, and he died.

literal: Chang was deep, keen, and had courage and resource; skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the West.
idiomatic: Chang was deep and keen, bold and resourceful, and skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to general who pacifies the west.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan; Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to Military Inspector.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan. Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to military inspector.

literal: With the generals on punitive campaigns he again followed Gao Huan in attacking the various bandits, rising in succession to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of a Government Office, Duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.
idiomatic: On punitive campaigns with the generals he again followed Gao Huan against the bandits, rising in succession to grand general of chariots and cavalry, opener of a government office, duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.

literal: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying: "Since I have garrisoned Heyang, I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know well all the strategic points."
idiomatic: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying, "Since I garrisoned Heyang I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know every strategic point."

literal: "Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. In the middle lies open country of a hundred and fifty li; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road."
idiomatic: "Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. Between them lies open country a hundred and fifty li across; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road."

literal: "I humbly propose selecting a place of natural advantage there, building garrison walls, stationing troops and horses, and cutting off their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."
idiomatic: "I humbly propose that we choose a place of natural advantage there, build garrison walls, station troops and horses, and cut their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."

literal: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.

literal: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made Grand Mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.
idiomatic: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made grand mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.

literal: Posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Tutor, chief of the first tribally enrolled division, prince in title, posthumous title Zhongwu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made director of the masters of writing, duke of the department of state affairs, grand tutor, and chief of the first tribally enrolled division, with princely rank in title and the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

literal: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was a native of Anding.
idiomatic: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was a native of Anding.

literal: By nature he was fierce and heroic and prized spirit and chivalry.
idiomatic: By nature he was fierce and heroic and prized spirit and chivalry.

literal: In Zhenguang of Wei, bandits rose in Longyou; an edict ordered Governor of Yong Province Yuan Meng to suppress them and recruited men of Langjia as army guides; Zuo answered the call.
idiomatic: In Zhenguang of Wei, bandits rose in Longyou; an edict ordered Governor of Yong Province Yuan Meng to suppress them and recruited Langjia men as army guides; Zuo answered the call.

literal: For military merit he rose in succession to General of Soaring Dragon and governor of Ling Province.
idiomatic: For military merit he rose in succession to general of soaring dragon and governor of Ling Province.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianzhong led the forces of Guanxi and, with Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianzhong led the forces of Guanxi and, with Erzhu Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.

literal: Tianzhong left Zuo in Eastern Qin, with overall command of three provinces and responsibility for pacifying two provinces.
idiomatic: Tianzhong left Zuo in Eastern Qin with overall command of three provinces and charge of pacifying two.

literal: When Tianzhong was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: When Tianzhong was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made grand general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, as grand commander he followed in breaking the Western army.
idiomatic: At the battle of Mount Mang he followed as grand commander in breaking the Western army.

literal: Zuo was made governor of Hua Province, with added opener of a government office equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies, and was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Linji county; he died.
idiomatic: Zuo was made governor of Hua Province, with added opener of a government office equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies, and was separately enfeoffed viscount of Linji county; he died.

literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made minister of works.

literal: Wei Zican, styled Huimao, was a native of Jingzhao.
idiomatic: Wei Zican, styled Huimao, was a native of Jingzhao.

literal: His great-grandfather Lang was Wei administrator of Xianyang.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Lang was Wei administrator of Xianyang.

literal: His father Juan was commissioner of waterways.
idiomatic: His father Juan was commissioner of waterways.

literal: Zican served as merit clerk of the commandery and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianzhong in pacifying Guanxi.
idiomatic: Zican served as the commandery merit clerk and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianzhong in pacifying Guanxi.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Zican was made governor of Southern Fen Province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Zican was made governor of Southern Fen Province.

literal: Gao Huan ordered generals out to attack; the city fell, and sons and younger brothers were all captured and sent to Jinyang, where they were spared and released.
idiomatic: Gao Huan ordered generals out to attack; the city fell, and sons and younger brothers were all captured and sent to Jinyang, where they were spared and released.

literal: Zican was made chief clerk of Bing Province and rose in succession to governor of Yu Province; he died.
idiomatic: Zican was made chief clerk of Bing Province and rose in succession to governor of Yu Province; he died.

literal: At first Zican had thirteen brothers, and with sons, nephews, and kin of the whole gate a hundred mouths all were in Western Wei.
idiomatic: At first Zican had thirteen brothers; with sons, nephews, and kin, the whole gate counted a hundred mouths, all in Western Wei.

literal: Because Zican, when the city fell, could not die in loyalty, many were put to death; after returning to the state only he and his younger brother Dao Xie survived.
idiomatic: Because Zican did not die when the city fell, many of his kin were put to death; after he returned to the Northern Qi state, only he and his younger brother Dao Xie survived.

literal: Xie entered the state together with Zican.
idiomatic: Xie had entered the state together with Zican.

literal: After Zican grew rich and noble, he then deliberately cast off Dao Xie, made him live apart, and in grain and salary scarcely shared with him — such was his disregard for kindness and righteousness.
idiomatic: After Zican grew rich and noble, he deliberately cast off Dao Xie, made him live apart, and scarcely shared his grain and salary with him — such was his disregard for kindness and righteousness.

literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
